text:
The switch from API key to Jellyfin credential sign-in happened because Seerr only lets an administrator mint an API key, and that key is instance-wide rather than per-user. The plugin's owner is a normal user on the target instance, so no key was obtainable.

During development the owner temporarily turned OFF auto-approve on their Seerr account so the end-to-end test could create real requests and then delete them. Seerr only lets a non-administrator delete their own request while its status is PENDING. If auto-approve is switched back on, every request that account creates is approved instantly and the cancel_request tool will return HTTP 401 for all of them. That is the account's configuration, not a plugin bug.
